name: Battle rifleman, JAP (our own design)
about: Made by Tools/battle_units/soldier.py. Metres; x forward, y right, z up. Paints: 0 tunic, 1 trousers, 2 boots, 3 lower, 4 straps, 5 helmet, 6 pack, 7 skin, 8 wood, 9 steel, 10 coat, 11 coat_dark, 12 leather, 13 blanket, 14 hoof (the eyes are painted as boots). near = LOD0, mid = LOD1, far = LOD2, all in the rest pose (arms 45 degrees down). Each point rides on bone `part` and, by `w2` (0 to 0.5), on bone `part2`. Skinning: a bone's turn G = G_parent * q (q from the clip, identity at rest; G of a bone with no track is its parent's), its head X = X_parent + G_parent * (head - head_parent + move), and a point p on it goes to X + G * (p - head). Quaternions are [t, w, x, y, z] in these axes (as Unreal's FQuat). Clips are in place: `stride` is the metres one loop covers; the game moves the unit. A mesh may carry `shade` per point (0 to 1, the wear and seam darkening): its colour is the paint's colour times shade; with no `shade` every point is 1.

stretcher_front.from: field_clips.py: this file's walk (motion capture), slowed and shortened, the arms keyed to the poles
stretcher_front.about: The front man of a two-man stretcher (the Stretcher prop, battle-models/ground-props), walking at about 0.73 m/s (stride 1.034 m a 1.42 s cycle), head down, the prop's grip.front.left/right in his fists: `grips` (his left fist then his right, every key, the root's frame, the game's axes; `mean` their average). Play stretcher_front and stretcher_rear on one clock (same phase, in step). Place the prop's root at the mean of the four fists less 0.14 m, head end (+x) toward the front man; then his root x = the prop's x + 1.1 - his grips' mean x. The carried man (carried_wounded) at the prop's `lie`. The rifle rides slung on his back.

stretcher_rear.from: field_clips.py: this file's walk (motion capture), slowed and shortened, the arms keyed to the poles
stretcher_rear.about: The rear man of a two-man stretcher (the Stretcher prop, battle-models/ground-props), walking at about 0.73 m/s (stride 1.034 m a 1.42 s cycle), head down, the prop's grip.back.left/right in his fists: `grips` (his left fist then his right, every key, the root's frame, the game's axes; `mean` their average). Play stretcher_front and stretcher_rear on one clock (same phase, in step). Place the prop's root at the mean of the four fists less 0.14 m, head end (+x) toward the front man; then his root x = the prop's x - 1.1 - his grips' mean x. The carried man (carried_wounded) at the prop's `lie`. The rifle rides slung on his back.

splice_kneel.from: field_clips.py: kneel_down's last pose, the arms keyed
splice_kneel.about: The lineman at a cut wire, kneeling (kneel_down, then this, then stand_up), twisting the two ends together in his hands three times and giving it a tug (event wire_tug) to test it. The wire's two ends run into his fists at `hands` (left then right, the root's frame, the game's axes): draw each end from there down to the ground and away along the line. His reel sits on the ground by his right knee. The rifle rides slung on his back.

carried_wounded.about: The man on the stretcher, alive (the dead stay still; he does not): on his back, head to +x (the Stretcher prop's head end, carried first), breathing, his left knee drawn up and let down, his right hand on his chest, his head turning now and then. His root goes at the prop's `lie` socket, turned with it. No weapon (the weapon bone rides 2 m under his root). His white field dressing is the game's to place.

reel_walk.from: field_clips.py: this file's walk (motion capture), slowed and shortened, bent, the arms keyed to the reel
reel_walk.about: The lineman walking his line out, about 0.73 m/s (stride 1.034 m a 1.42 s cycle), bent forward, the CableReel prop (battle-models/ground-props) carried before him by its two handles: `reel` gives, every key, the prop's root (x, y, z) and his left and right fists (on its grip.left and grip.right), the root's frame, the game's axes; the prop faces as he does. Turn its drum by the wire paid out (the prop's README). The rifle rides slung on his back.

wounded_waiting.about: A wounded man on the ground waiting for the bearers, alive: on his back (head to +x, his root on the ground under his middle), breathing hard, his right hand pressed to the wound at his right side, his left knee drawn up and let down, his head turning, and once a loop his left arm lifted to call them. His rifle lies by his right side. When the bearers reach him: carried_wounded on the stretcher (the same lie, so it swaps without a jump but for the hands).

about_variety: Variety (Tools/battle_units/variety.py and helmet_finishes.py): one man made into many. `faces` (8): face 0 is the man as he is; for face k, add `move` (metres, this file's axes) to the points listed in `at`, at each level of detail, then colour: every skin-painted point's colour times `tone`, and each point in `tint_at` times its `tint` (the hair, brows, stubble or moustache), all on top of the paint (and `shade`) as usual. `helmets`: his helmet (or cap, ushanka or hood) in the finishes it was worn in. Each is a rigid mesh at near/mid/far in the same form as the file's own meshes (points, facings, paints, triangles, part, part2, w2, and shade where the file has it), with `ink` at each point: -1 paints the point by its paint number as ever; any other value is an index into `inks` (colours, RRGGBB), the colour to paint it instead. To draw a man in a finish, leave out his own helmet's triangles, `helmet_tris[lod]` = [first, count] (they are the last of the list), and draw the finish's mesh skinned on the same bones. Each finish has `season` (any, summer, winter), `front` (any, east, west, south, desert, pacific, china) and `share` (how common it was), and no `from` or `to` month (Brian's standing rule, 26 November 2026: a man's markings and paint never hang on the year). Picking, for each man: the finishes whose season and front fit (any fits all), whatever the battle's date, one chosen by share, and face = a hash of (block id, k) mod 8 and the helmet from another hash of the same, so a man keeps both all battle. When no finish fits his season and front, he wears his own helmet in his army's helmet colour. No swastika, rising-sun flag or fascist badge is drawn: the German eagle decal is left off (its side stays plain paint).
about_deaths: Deaths (Tools/battle_units/falls.py on ragdoll.py): every die_* clip named in `deaths` is a physics fall baked from this man's own body (his parts' masses, his joints' human ranges, the muscle tone going out of him, the ground under him; the rifle leaves his hand and lands where it lands), so no two kinds fall alike and none sinks into the ground. Pick: deaths[stance][kind], stance stand, run, kneel, prone or cover (what he was doing when hit), kind as the Fates picker's man_fall kinds (forward, back, side, knees, spin, thrown) or crawl (wounded: he falls, drags himself on a little, then goes still), or where he was hit when the scene knows it: head (he drops where he stands), gut (he folds at the waist, then goes down), leg (that leg goes from under him); one of the list by a hash of (block id, man). Play it once (loop false) and hold its last frame for the rest of the battle: the body stays where it fell. Each clip starts in the pose of `start` [clip, time] (blend into it over ~0.15 s from whatever he was doing); `end_offset` is where his pelvis ends (metres, his own axes; the clip is not in place: the pelvis and the rifle move); the weapon bone's last key is the rifle lying on the ground. Events: knee_down, body_fall, rifle_drop (and elbow_down in a crawl), at the time they touch. The older die_back, die_forward and die_kneel stay in the file as they were but are not in the table (they sink into the ground).
about_wear: Wear and weather (Tools/battle_units/shade.py; Brian, 22 November 2026: uniforms dirtier the longer a unit is at the front, fresh replacements clean; rain darkens the cloth and splashes the mud higher; snow white on the shoulders and helmets). Per point, at near, mid and far and on each helmet finish's own mesh: `shade` (0.4 to 1) and `tint` (3 a point: red, green, blue) are the look as baked, a man some weeks in the line (wear W 0.6) in dry weather, for drawing paint x shade x tint as ever. `shade_clean`: the same shadow with no dirt (folds, under the straps, pack, belt and helmet brim, worn edges, the cloth's uneven fade). `dirt` (0 to 1): where dust and mud collect in dry weather (boots, leggings and trousers to a little over the knee in splashes, the knees, the seat, elbows, cuffs and hands, a little in the face's creases); `dirt_wet`: the same in rain (mud splashed up the thighs, caked boots, heavier knees and seat, the forearms and the front of the belly from going down in it). `wet` (0 to 1): how much the surface darkens when soaked (wool 1, webbing 0.8, leather 0.6, wood 0.45, helmet paint 0.3, steel 0.2, skin 0.15; less under the pack and the arms). `snow` (0 to 1): how much snow settles there on a man standing (open to the sky and facing up: the helmet's crown, shoulders, pack, the tops of the arms and boots; little on skin and steel). MIXING, per man: W = wear, from how long his unit has been at the front (0.1 a fresh replacement or a new unit, 1 six weeks or more in the line; replacements in a veteran unit stay low until they have been in it a while), R = rain (0 dry ground to 1 soaked) and S = snow (0 to 1), both from the battle's weather draw. In sRGB 0 to 1: base = paint x shade_clean x (1 - 0.35 x wet x R) (x the face's tone and tint); d = (dirt + (dirt_wet - dirt) x R) x W; soil = (DUST + (MUD - DUST) x R) x shade_clean, DUST (0.60, 0.54, 0.43) dry dust and dried mud, MUD (0.27, 0.21, 0.15) wet mud (or the field's own soil, lighter dry); colour = base + (soil - base) x 0.85 x d; then toward snow (0.92, 0.94, 0.97) x (0.6 + 0.4 x shade_clean) by 0.9 x snow x S. The gore paints (wound, bone, blood): shade 1, no dirt, wet or snow. Mid and far carry the near's, their shade eased off (90 % and 75 % of the darkening).

face_mesh.about: Close-range face (Tools/battle_units/face_mesh.py): the near mesh's face is split finer, red-green (no crack), and its new points set on MakeHuman's man the file was cut from (seed and nation below), so lids, lips, nostrils and the folds by the nose come back; the eyeballs' fronts are split once on their own spheres. No index moves: a split triangle keeps its place with its first piece; the other pieces and the new points are on the end of near's lists (from the first new point and triangle below), so helmet_tris and the gore ranges stay true. Each new point takes its parents' bone weights, shade, wear and tint, and in each face their move, facing and tint. Mid and far are as they were.

about_run_styles: run_styles.py (release 2, 23 November 2026): run_b, run_c, run_d and advance_b, advance_c, advance_d, each another runner's motion capture (CMU 09_02, 16_36, 09_03) with this file's own hold on his weapon; style_of names the clip each is a style of; the feet planted on this file's legs, the stride fitted to them (a planted foot slides no more than in his own run). The game gives each man one of the four (LandMen, the run-styles switch); far men banked in poses play the base clip's.

ride_clips.places: each clip's `places` (and by_vehicle here): the vehicle's socket moved by root_offset (forward, right, up of the socket's facing, the game's axes); the clip's root goes there, facing as the socket does. A seat's root is the seat's point (anchor `seat`); the Jeep's gunner's is the floor at his feet (anchor `feet`). Loops are 4 s; the deaths 2.4 s, the last pose held from 1.5 s (play once and hold). Each car seat has exactly one death in its `places`, falling to the car's outer side (away from the man beside him): die_seat_slump (driver, folds to his left) and die_seat_slump_r (the right-hand-drive Fiat 508 and Kurogane drivers, to his right); die_ride_slump (a passenger on the car's right, slumps to his right) and die_ride_slump_l (a passenger on the left, to his left). Find a seat's death by the death clips' `places`, as you find its loop.
ride_clips.weapon: `weapon`: `none` the rifle put away 2 m under his feet (hide the weapon, bolt and bipod triangles, as for the tank crew); `slung` on his back, drawn; `rifle` stood between his knees in his hands, drawn (car_ride, car_ride_back, die_ride_slump, die_ride_slump_l).
ride_clips.turn_with_gun: jeep_gunner, sidecar_gunner and sidecar_gunner_b hold the gun's grips (grip.gunner.l/.r): if the game turns the gun on its mount (mg_mount), turn the man with it about the mount's upright axis.
ride_clips.grip_labels: the cars' grip.driver.l is on the driver's right and .r on his left (the clips take each hand from where the grips are, so nothing needs changing); the motorcycles' bar grips are on their steering part: if the game turns the bars, the hands are where the bars are straight.
ride_clips.far: the far pose bank (pose_bank.json) has no seated poses: draw riders with the near or mid meshes.
ride_clips.trucks: The benches in the back of the Truck, the Hanomag and the M3 (rider.1-10: rider.1-5 on her left bench facing her right, rider.6-10 on the right): bench_ride is each seat's loop (4 s), his rifle stood between his knees in both hands; die_bench_slump its death (2.4 s, held from 1.5: he folds forward over his knees inside his own place). bench_rise_* gets him up turning toward the way out, ending upright in the aisle facing aft, his rifle at the port; bench_sit_* is the way back down, from standing in the aisle facing forward. aisle.<vehicle>.seats names each seat's rise and sit (the M3's front pair and both half-tracks' rear pair have their own: the M3's machine gun over the aisle, the stern and its rolled canvas just behind the rear pair). Walk him along her floor (aisle.floor_z) from where the rise leaves him to aisle.way_out.start, facing aft; empty the rear seats first. Then play one of aisle.way_out.clips at the `step` socket with its root_offset (as any place): these carry root motion (the root track: the root under his boots, from her floor onto the ground; its last key is where he stands, aisle.way_out.clips.<clip>.ends_at in her own axes): hand him to the ground battle's walking there. Play her `dismount` clip first (the board or doors open: the ways out are checked so). The Truck carries men with her tilt stowed (swap `tilt` off).

way_out.open_first: play her `dismount` clip (it opens the tailboard) before the first man reaches the start

Truck.headroom: under her tilt 1.59 m over the floor, its rear opening 1.45: she carries men with it stowed (swap tilt off); a man under it creeps (head under 1.45)

way_out.open_first: play her `dismount` clip (it opens the stern doors) before the first man reaches the start

Hanomag.headroom: open-topped; the canvas rolled across the top of her stern is 1.18 over the floor at the doors: out_doors_* duck under it from their start

way_out.open_first: play her `dismount` clip (it opens the stern door) before the first man reaches the start

M3Halftrack.headroom: open-topped; her machine gun stands over the aisle 0.94-1.15 over the floor from 0.95 behind its pedestal (x -0.95) to the cab; the canvas rolled across the top of her stern is only 0.79 over the floor at the door: out_door_* squat under it from their start

check.how: light_riders.py check_all on the pattern man, every 8th frame of 60 a second, against each vehicle's mesh (crew.check with the nine-ray overlap test; the sidecar tubs by tub_check): how deep any point of him goes into the vehicle, and his hands' gap to their grips. The Kübelwagen and Kurogane are the mended seat-fix models. truck_riders.py check_all on the pattern man the same way, at every bench seat and way out (the Truck with her tilt stowed; the ways out with her board or doors opened as her dismount clip leaves them).

about_riders: light_riders.py and light_riders_fit.py (release 2, 23 November 2026): the men who ride the light vehicles (jeeps, field cars, motorcycles and sidecars, battle-models/land/vehicles/): a clip for each seat and a death for each, made on one pattern man at the vehicles' own seat sockets and grips and fitted to this man (his arms and legs reach the same grips, pedals and footrests). `ride_clips` says which clip goes at which seat. Each clip's root goes at its seat socket moved by its root_offset (forward, right, up of the socket's facing, the game's axes), as the tank crew's commander_hatch goes at its hatch. Each car seat's death falls to the car's outside (die_seat_slump/_r for the driver, die_ride_slump/_l for a passenger), so two men side by side never slump onto each other. Fitted to the mended Kübelwagen and Kurogane seats (the seat-fix models). With them (truck_riders.py, the same way): the men on the benches in the back of the Truck, the Hanomag and the M3 half-track (bench_ride and its death, getting up toward the way out and sitting down), and their ways out over the Truck's tailboard and through the half-tracks' stern doors (out_*, with root motion).

bail_clips.order: bail_climb_out at the commander's hatch, then (where the turret stands over the hull's deck) bail_step_down at the turret's edge, then bail_jump_down at the edge of the hull, then the ground battle's own run away; a man on fire plays burning_run (looped, moved by its stride) and then burning_fall_roll.
bail_clips.climb: bail_climb_out (1.5 s): its root at the tank's `commander` socket moved by root_offset (0, 0, -0.92: his boots 0.92 m under the socket, stood in the hatch as commander_hatch; its `places` name the Sherman, Panzer IV and Tiger, where it is checked), facing as the socket does. The root track takes him up 0.95 m onto the turret's roof, 0.47 m to his right and 0.10 m forward: on a roof higher or lower than 0.95 m over where his boots began (the Panzer IV's 0.82, the Tiger's 0.97, the Sherman's 1.07) add the difference to his height from 0.8 s on (his knee on the roof).
bail_clips.step: bail_step_down (0.73 s): from standing at the edge of the turret's roof facing out, 0.95 m over where he lands: off the edge at 0.10 s, down at 0.55 s, on bent knees, his left hand back onto the turret's edge (the roof at his shoulder then). Walk him from where bail_climb_out leaves him to the turret's edge with the ground battle's walk. Root track: down 0.95 m, forward 0.42 m. From a higher or lower drop, add the difference to his height between 0.10 s and 0.55 s. His pelvis's track is from the root, as in every clip with root motion: it comes down with it.
bail_clips.jump: bail_jump_down (1.60 s): from standing at the edge of the hull's top facing out, 1.50 m over where he lands: off the edge at 0.44 s, down at 1.09 s, on bent knees, his right hand going down to the ground, then up into his first running stride. Walk him from where bail_step_down (or bail_climb_out) leaves him to the hull's edge. Root track: down 1.50 m, forward 1.71 m. From a higher or lower drop, add the difference to his height between 0.44 s and 1.09 s. His pelvis's track is from the root, as in every clip with root motion: it comes down with it.
bail_clips.burning: burning_run (2.1 s loop, in place): `stride` 7.35 m a loop (3.5 m a second): move him that much. burning_fall_roll (3.8 s, play once and hold the last pose; still from 3.3 s): starts from burning_run's first frame (blend into it from wherever the run is); its root track is the ground under his pelvis (0.95 m forward and 1.20 m to his right at the end: he rolls to his right).
bail_clips.weapon: `weapon` none in all four: put away 2 m under his feet (hide the weapon, bolt and bipod triangles, as for the tank crew's clips).
bail_clips.far: the far pose bank (pose_bank.json) has none of these poses: draw them with the near or mid meshes.

check.how: tank_bail.py on the pattern man: at each tank's hatch, the deepest of him into the tank over the rim (crew.check) and into the hatch's ring (tank_crew.cupola_check), his hands' gap to the rim; the lowest of him under the ground (or the roof, or the hull's top while he is on it); the fastest any bone turns (degrees between keys at 30 a second).

about_bail: tank_bail.py and light_riders_fit.py (release 2, 23 November 2026; Brian: "if a tank gets hit people try and get out before it explodes"): a knocked-out tank's crew getting out, for the battle's bail-out (Battle/LandBail.cpp): up out of the commander's hatch (bail_climb_out), down off the hull (bail_jump_down), and a man on fire running (burning_run), then falling and rolling (burning_fall_roll). Made once on one pattern man (crew.py's, the German rifleman), the climb checked against the Sherman's, the Panzer IV's and the Tiger's own hatches, and fitted to this man (his arms and legs reach the same rim, roof and ground). His weapon is put away in all four. `bail_clips` says where and how to play them.
about_pack: pack_tris (pack_range.py): his pack and all his webbing (belt, straps, pouches, bags, canteen, shovel, bayonet, gas-mask can, rolls, a radio or aid bags), one run of triangles at each level [first, count], as helmet_tris: leave it out for a man with no pack (a downed pilot, a crew out of a tank) and draw nothing in its place, the cloth is whole under it. Buttons, badges, the helmet's chin strap and the weapon are not in it.

far_mend.about: far level's body re-made by far_mend.py (24 November 2026, release 2): cut down from the middle level's body to the old far body's size (the old one had been torn into sheets); kit, rifle and helmet as before.
